https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cy07.text: Image source, Reuters By Jamie Whitehead Published 9 hours ago The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the biggest in the country's history, the World Health Organization (WHO) has said. As of 30 July, there were 3,605 confirmed cases including 1,587 deaths - a fatality rate of 44%. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus. It was declared on 15 May 2026 and surpasses the previous biggest outbreak between 2018 and 2020, which had nearly 3,500 recorded cases of whom almost 2,300 died. There is currently no approved vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain, but vaccines are being developed in the UK and Singapore. Ebola, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids, has killed 15,000 people across Africa over the last 50 years. The WHO said in a statement posted on X , external that the outbreak was "intensifying, with sustained transmission and continued increases in reported cases and deaths". It added that during the past week, the outbreak reached its highest weekly total with 567 cases and 296 deaths. It warned these figures underscored "the exceptional pace of transmission". "Factors like insecurity, population displacement, and cross-border movement continue to hamper response efforts and increase the risk of further spread," it said. The centre of the outbreak is the Ituri province in the northeast of the country, which borders South Sudan and Uganda. But it has also spread to other parts of the country, including the North and South Kivu provinces, where large areas are controlled by the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group. "The convergence of insecurity, population displacement and mobility, and cross-border movements complicate response operations and increase the risk of further geographical spread," the WHO said. Published 16 July DR Congo takes Rwanda to international court over decades of conflict Published 26 June During the current outbreak, 20 cases have also been reported in Uganda along with one in France. Two cases diagnosed in DR Congo were later treated in Germany. On 30 July, the WHO announced that the the "most promising" vaccine would be developed in Singapore, while the trail of a separate jab has begun in the UK. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/horror-ww.text: Rebecca Robinson Updated Wed, 22 July 2026 at 10:50 am UTC 0 Putin reportedly has his sights set on four new targets. (Image: Getty) Vladimir Putin is reportedly eyeing up four new targets as he struggles to secure a victory over Ukraine. Lithuania's Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said the Russian president could turn his attention to the Baltic states - Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia - and Poland. He claimed that uncertainties over the outcome of the four-year-long Ukraine war have caused the Russian people to question and turn on their government, leaving Putin scrambling for a win. Mr Kaunas told LRT: "Since the war in Ukraine is not unfolding as Russia planned, they are unable to win, and today explosions are echoing within Russia itself, there are fuel shortages... There are fears that Russia could target the Baltics and Poland. (Image: Getty) "Russian society is already questioning the Kremlin regime about why this is happening and where the promised victory is. "The Kremlin, Putin, needs a new escalation, some kind of new win, and the Baltic region and Poland are the nearest targets in this case." Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausda added that Russia is planning to escalate in Poland or the Baltic states to test NATO. The Kremlin recently rejected such claims, branding them "the latest batch of ‌scare stories designed to continue brainwashing the population and preparing it for further militarisation". However, Mr Nausda told BNS that intelligence data indicates concerns about possible attacks on critical infrastructure using conventional military or hybrid tactics. In response, the country has stepped up security around critical transport and energy infrastructure, including bridges, electricity substations, gas supply systems, and communications hubs. Plans are also being made in response to a potential Russian attack, LRT reports. Polish Foreign Minister Radosaw Sikorski also suggested Russia could stage a false flag operation using Ukrainian drones. The country was recently forced to scramble fighter jets to intercept a Russian Il-20 aircraft over the Baltic Sea. The Russian plane had no filed flight plan and with its transponder turned off. The aircraft was carrying out a reconnaissance mission in international airspace, the Polish Operational Command of the Armed Forces said. The on-duty pair of Air Force fighters successfully intercepted, visually identified, and escorted the aircraft away from the area of responsibility. Trending WEIRTON - One Weirton church celebrated its history and contributions to the community during almost a century of service. Shiloh Apostolic Faith Assembly welcomed members - past and present - along with other guests from the community on Sunday to celebrate the 98th anniversary of the church. Sunday's celebration featured a theme of "Journey On," with services reflecting on verses from Deuteronomy and Nehemiah, stressing the importance of God's work in the world. "We believe we still have a purpose in the community," said Bishop Darrell Cummings, pastor of the church located on Weir Avenue, noting the church wants to continue to make a difference. "We're living in an age where a number of churches are closing, merging or going virtual." Evangelist Latisha Cummings led one of the first presentations, with prayers, songs, and a reflection on the theme of the day, inspired by Deuteronomy 31: 1-8 "The Lord Himself goes before you and will be with you; He will never leave you nor forsake you." Rebecca Turner is the second of five generations who have attended Shiloh, noting many of the songs and reflections during the celebration were done in remembrance of long-time members, many of whom were part of the church's early days. "A lot of them, when they died, were over 90 years old," she said. "It sums up a long lifeline." The program included references of church leaders Roosevelt Roseberry, Inella Alsbrooks, Sallie Sims, Eva Wilks, Mattie Bradshaw, Gussie Burns, Willie Williams, and Alice Johnson. Shiloh traces its history to the late 1920s, initially with tent services on Sixth Street in Weirton's north end. A formal location was established in 1928 in a small store front on Avenue A. Baptisms would be held in the Ohio River. A series of acting pastors would serve until 1937, when Elder J.J. Gibson was installed. Helen Jeter, one of Gibson's daughters and one of the church's senior members, recalled her father's work and talents. "He played a mean guitar," Jeter said, recalling he often would play during services. Under Gibson's leadership, a fund drive was held in the 1940s to purchase the former Polish Hall on Avenue A and convert it into a church. In the 1970s, with service to 30 families and the expansion of Weirton Steel, discussions were held of building a new church, eventually moving to Weir Avenue in 1980. "We had services starting out in the basement, then moved upstairs," Turner noted. Gibson would pastor at Shiloh for more than 50 years, then followed by Elder Paul Moore in 1987, Elder Johnnie Edwards in 1998, with Cummings installed as pastor around 2004. Sunday's event also included a service led by Suffragan Bishop James Agnew III of Tree of Life Church in Martins Ferry, as well as a community dinner. Starting at /week. Subscribe Today

https://www.g4media.ro/ft-reprezentati-a.text: Funcționăm ca organizație non-profit, iar banii rezultați din contribuțiile cititorilor sunt destinați integral finanțării proiectului G4Media. Consilieri de rang înalt din Franța, Germania și Regatul Unit, precum și reprezentanți ai Comisiei Europene și NATO, vor participa marți și miercuri la o parte dintre discuțiile privind războiul din Ucraina, organizate la Abu Dhabi, relatează Financial Times . Prezența europenilor urmărește să consolideze poziția de negociere a Kievului și să împiedice Rusia să folosească tratativele mediate de Statele Unite pentru a obține influență asupra arhitecturii de securitate a Europei. La reuniuni vor lua parte consilierii pentru securitate națională ai Franței, Germaniei și Regatului Unit, precum și șefii de cabinet ai președintei Comisiei Europene și secretarului general al NATO, potrivit unor surse familiarizate cu pregătirile. Discuțiile de la Abu Dhabi au fost concepute inițial ca negocieri trilaterale între Statele Unite, Rusia și Ucraina, în cadrul eforturilor administrației președintelui Donald Trump de a pune capăt războiului declanșat de invazia rusă din februarie 2022. Însă implicarea europeană a devenit o prioritate după ce Trump și emisarul său pentru pace, Jared Kushner, au sugerat săptămâna trecută că un nou cadru de securitate pentru întregul continent ar putea face parte dintr-un eventual acord. Inițiativa a stârnit îngrijorări în capitalele europene, în condițiile în care Rusia solicită de mult timp să aibă un cuvânt de spus în decizii care țin de suveranitatea statelor europene, precum exercițiile NATO, desfășurarea trupelor și amplasarea sistemelor de armament în Europa de Est. Guvernele europene consideră inacceptabilă o asemenea influență a Moscovei, pe care o asociază cu revenirea la sferele de influență din perioada Războiului Rece. Potrivit unor oficiali citați de Financial Times, referirea lui Kushner la un nou cadru de securitate postbelic pentru Europa nu a fost discutată în prealabil cu guvernele europene. Acestea insistă că orice negociere privind securitatea continentului, dincolo de problema Ucrainei, trebuie să aibă loc după discuțiile de pace cu Kievul, nu în paralel cu acestea. „În ultimele săptămâni, europenii și-au făcut auzită vocea, exprimându-i mediatorului american faptul că nicio discuție privind viitorul continentului nu poate ignora așteptările și cerințele noastre”, a declarat luni ministrul francez de Externe, Jean-Noël Barrot, pentru postul RTL. Programul detaliat al reuniunilor de la Abu Dhabi nu a fost făcut public. Discuțiile ar urma să se desfășoare în mai multe formate, în funcție de subiectele abordate și de participanți. Pentru reprezentanții europeni, cele mai importante teme sunt garanțiile de securitate care ar urma să fie oferite Ucrainei și planul de redresare economică a țării după război. Participarea reprezentanților europeni are loc în contextul dificultăților cu care s-au confruntat guvernele de pe continent în încercarea de a stabili cine vorbește în numele Europei în dosarul ucrainean și care ar trebui să fie poziția comună a statelor europene, după revenirea lui Donald Trump la Casa Albă. Problema s-a accentuat în ultimele săptămâni, pe măsură ce emisarii americani și-au intensificat eforturile diplomatice pentru încheierea războiului. Săptămâna trecută, premierul italian Giorgia Meloni a criticat dur modul „dezorganizat și necoordonat” în care Europa și-a gestionat implicarea în negocieri. Liderii Uniunii Europene urmează să discute despre o mai bună coordonare a poziției comune în cadrul unui summit programat vineri. Delegația ucraineană la Abu Dhabi va fi condusă de Rustem Umerov, șeful serviciului de informații externe al Ucrainei. Rusia va fi reprezentată de viceministrul de Externe Serghei Riabkov și de Vladimir Medinski, consilier al Kremlinului. Articol editat de un jurnalist în care au fost folosite texte traduse cu AI.
